source_user: Calculation case 144: a model has 48 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 2560, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 48 × 2560 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 503316480 bytes = 0.468750 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: dense (non-MLA) transformer with GQA, 8 KV heads shared across query heads; K and V stored separately at BF16/FP16 (2 byte(s) per element); one sequence of 2560 tokens fully cached; no quantization scales, no page/block padding, no allocator overhead counted.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x sequence_length x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_element.

Substitution: 2 x 48 x 2560 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 503316480 bytes = 480.000 MiB = 0.468750 GiB.

Boundary conditions and falsifiable points:
- Paged attention (vLLM PagedAttention, block_size 16 or 32) rounds each sequence up to whole blocks, so real occupancy is ceil(2560/block)*block tokens, up to a few percent higher.
- If KV is quantized to INT8/FP8 the per-channel or per-block scale/zero-point tensors add roughly 1/block_size extra bytes and are NOT in this number.
- Under tensor parallelism of degree TP, KV heads are sharded, so per-GPU bytes are about total/TP only when 8 % TP == 0; otherwise the runtime replicates KV heads and per-GPU bytes are higher than total/TP.
- MLA (DeepSeek-style) or cross-layer KV sharing invalidates this formula entirely; it would give a large over-estimate.
- Speculative decoding and beam search multiply live KV by the number of draft/beam branches.

Evidence to confirm: read config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim or hidden_size/num_attention_heads) rather than trusting the prompt; then compare against measured steady-state GPU memory, e.g. vLLM's reported num_gpu_blocks x block_size x per-token KV bytes, or nvidia-smi / torch.cuda.memory_allocated deltas across one request.

Capacity gate: concurrency is limited by (KV budget after weights and activations) / 503316480 bytes per full-length sequence. Roll back or reduce max_num_seqs / max_model_len if measured KV bytes exceed this estimate by more than ~10 percent, which indicates padding, replication or a wrong head count.
risks: Formula ignores paged-attention block padding, so it under-estimates real allocator footprint.
No mention that TP sharding of KV heads may not divide evenly, causing KV replication.
Assumes standard GQA KV cache; silently wrong for MLA or cross-layer KV sharing architectures.
Quantized-KV cases omit scale/zero-point overhead.

risks: Formula ignores paged-attention block padding, so it under-estimates real allocator footprint.
No mention that TP sharding of KV heads may not divide evenly, causing KV replication.
Assumes standard GQA KV cache; silently wrong for MLA or cross-layer KV sharing architectures.
Quantized-KV cases omit scale/zero-point overhead.
evidence_required: model config.json: num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim
serving runtime KV block accounting (e.g. vLLM num_gpu_blocks x block_size)
measured GPU memory delta for a single full-length request
